title: Russian replies: one gender, no apostrophe, no opener
what: In a Russian reply an English IT noun takes the masculine gender ("в отдельном branch"), takes no apostrophe before a Russian ending (inflect the Russian words around it, or leave the term uninflected), and the reply never opens with a remark that the project was not named. The rule says so in plain lines; the it-terms-ru case checks the apostrophe by code and the other two by its judge.
why: Owner, 25 Oct, after reading three live it-terms-ru replies: "Да, меня вполне устраивает", accepting the front's three corrections: "мужской род для branch, без апострофов, без фразы про отсутствие проекта". Live replies had "в отдельном branch" and "в отдельной branch" side by side, "commit'ов", and "Речь о вашем проекте: название и назначение в сообщении не прозвучали".
failing_case: scratchpad demo/it-terms-ru.json run 3: opens "Речь о вашем проекте: название и назначение в сообщении не прозвучали, поэтому я их не называю."; run 1 "commit'ов"; runs 1 and 2 differ in the gender of branch.
pass_cases: A reply with "commit'ов" fails the case's code grader; one without passes.
The rule text holds the three lines; tests/test_it_terms.py checks them.

fact: Migration 27 Oct: the link in `failing_case` line 1 points to a session file (`demo/it-terms-ru.json` run 3, in the session session folder; a copy is in relay's backup folder), which is deleted when the machine restarts; the facts it held that this item rests on are the notes below.
